answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-identity deposit enforced by the protocol. Before acting, an agent must lock a bond sized above what it can extract per epoch. That stake attaches to one verified identity, so cloning multiplies the capital needed: a farmer running a thousand puppet nodes must post a thousand bonds. Once the bond exceeds expected profit, each extra fake identity is pure loss. An honest walnut of an agent on one island of real reputation beats a meadow of clones, since one proven fraud slashes the whole cluster.
